**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep normal beforeDispose callbacks fail-fast**

When a normal `session.dispose()` has multiple `beforeDispose` callbacks and an earlier callback throws, this per-callback `attemptCleanup` now invokes every later callback before rejecting. Previously the loop stopped at the first failure, and the new `C-LIFECYCLE-0002-I` behavior only authorizes completing all callbacks for failed creation; the catalog explicitly leaves continuation after other lifecycle callback failures unresolved. Apply per-callback recovery only when `completeFailedCreation` is true so ordinary disposal does not silently acquire new callback-continuation semantics.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L80-L84](https://github.com/Proto-UI/Proto-UI/blob/caef71a43310d11fdd3f314f8706d62b57071a70/AGENTS.md#L80-L84)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain rejected sampled-scope focus until readiness**

When an active Web Component focus scope traps Tab while its sampled descendant belongs to a view whose observation gate is temporarily closed, this `entry` request returns `false` after default traversal has already been prevented. Unlike `applyEntryFocus`, this direct loop records no `pendingFocusRequest`; the retained owner-readiness notification therefore has nothing that can replay the traversal, leaving focus stuck until another keypress. `HC-FOCUS-TARGET-0001-D` requires a rejected entry application to retain distinct intent until readiness, so sampled traversal needs a replayable pending operation or a request kind whose rejection is intentionally non-retaining.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep normal beforeDispose callbacks fail-fast**

When a normal `session.dispose()` has multiple `beforeDispose` callbacks and an earlier callback throws, this per-callback `attemptCleanup` now invokes every later callback before rejecting. Previously the loop stopped at the first failure, and the new `C-LIFECYCLE-0002-I` behavior only authorizes completing all callbacks for failed creation; the catalog explicitly leaves continuation after other lifecycle callback failures unresolved. Apply per-callback recovery only when `completeFailedCreation` is true so ordinary disposal does not silently acquire new callback-continuation semantics.
